source: English translation: Valmiki Ramayanam, IIT Kanpur (https://www.valmiki.iitk.ac.in/), via the MIT-licensed Valmiki Ramayan Dataset by Ashutosh Vijay.

verses.1: Having heard Rama's speech, Lakshmana, who knew the highest truth, spoke words with folded hands to Rama, who was radiant with splendor.
verses.2: O Kakutstha, for a minor offense, such a severe curse was given by the two Brahmins, like another punishment from Yama for the royal sage Nṛga.
verses.3: O best of men, what did King Nṛga say to the two enraged Brahmins after hearing himself accused of sin?
verses.4: When Lakshmana thus spoke, Rama again said, "O gentle one, listen to how that king was previously afflicted by the curse."
verses.5: Then, having understood that the two Brahmins had departed, King Nṛga summoned all his ministers, citizens, and priests.
verses.6: Deeply afflicted by sorrow, King Nṛga spoke to all of them, including his subjects, saying, "Let my words be heard by all of you with attention."
verses.7: The noble and blameless Narada and Parvata, having instilled great fear in me, have indeed departed to the three worlds, swift as the wind.
verses.8: Let this boy named Vasu be consecrated as a god today, and let artisans construct for me a pleasant cave where I can exhaust the curse issued by a Brahmin.
verses.9: The artisans should construct one cave that is rain-proof, another that is cold-proof, and a third, pleasant to touch, that is summer-proof.
verses.10: Let fruit-bearing trees, flowering creepers, and various kinds of shade-giving shrubs be planted.
verses.11: Let the surroundings of the caves be made beautiful in all directions, for I will dwell there comfortably until the end of my destined time.
verses.12: Let fragrant flowers always be placed in them, surrounding the area for me to a distance of one and a half Yojanas.
verses.13: Having made this arrangement, the king then instructed his son, "O son, ever devoted to righteousness, protect your subjects according to the duty of a Kshatriya."
verses.14: O best among men, you yourself witnessed how a curse was inflicted upon me by the two angry Brahmins, even for such an offense.
verses.15: O best of men, do not grieve for my sake, O son, for destiny is powerful, and it is by its force that I have been afflicted with this misery.
verses.16: One obtains only what is destined to be obtained, goes only where one is destined to go, and receives only the sorrows and joys that are destined to be received.
verses.17: O son, do not grieve over what happened in a former birth.
verses.18: O best among men, having thus spoken to his son, the highly renowned king went into the well, which was well-constructed for his dwelling.
verses.19: Having thus just entered that well adorned with great jewels, the great-souled king then fulfilled the curse that had indeed been uttered with anger by the two Brahmins. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुःपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 54 ।। Thus ends the fifty-fourth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
